subproblem.title: The upper n-density ratio limsup of an arbitrary measure is Borel measurable (supplied proof, step 1)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let μ be any measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra). For x ∈ ℝ^P let Θ*(x) := limsup_{ρ→0⁺} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n), the limsup taken in [0, ∞] along the filter 𝓝[>]0, where B_ρ(x) is the open ball and ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n (the quotient is ENNReal division by ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)). Then x ↦ Θ*(x).toReal is Borel measurable on ℝ^P. No finiteness assumption on μ is made.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), Measurable (fun x : Euclid P => (limsup (fun ρ : ℝ => μ (ball x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0)).toReal)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the selected node's supplied proof (class_reduction), which follows Simon 7.3.3, Remark 3.4 and the proof of 3.3(2) (chapter-07.txt lines 380–398 and 512–583) and Appendix A, A.1–A.4 (chapter-A.txt lines 18–45). This child is step 1 of that proof ("Measurability of dens μ, any measure μ"). Its lower semicontinuity claim is proved here by continuity from below instead of Fatou's lemma; both give the same fact.
Notation: c_ρ := ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) ∈ [0, ∞] and g_ρ(x) := μ(B_ρ(x))/c_ρ for ρ ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^P, so Θ*(x) = limsup_{𝓝[>]0} (ρ ↦ g_ρ(x)).
1. (0 < ω_n < ∞.) ω_n = volume(B_1(0)) with B_1(0) ⊆ ℝ^n = Euclid n. The volume on the finite-dimensional inner product space Euclid n is an additive Haar measure, so it is positive on nonempty open sets and finite on bounded sets. Hence ω_n ∈ (0, ∞). This includes n = 0, where Euclid 0 = {0} and B_1(0) = {0} is open and nonempty. Consequently, for ρ > 0, ρ^n > 0 and c_ρ ∈ (0, ∞).
2. (Lower semicontinuity of balls.) Fix ρ > 0. Then h_ρ(x) := μ(B_ρ(x)) ∈ [0, ∞] is lower semicontinuous in x. Let x ∈ ℝ^P and t < h_ρ(x). The open balls B_{s_m}(x) with s_m := ρ(1 − 1/(m+2)) increase with m, and their union is B_ρ(x). By continuity from below, μ(B_ρ(x)) = sup_m μ(B_{s_m}(x)) (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop for the monotone family), so t < μ(B_{s_m}(x)) for some m. If |x' − x| < ρ − s_m, then B_{s_m}(x) ⊆ B_ρ(x') (|z − x'| ≤ |z − x| + |x − x'| < s_m + (ρ − s_m)), so t < μ(B_ρ(x')). Hence {x' : t < h_ρ(x')} is a neighbourhood of x. This is lower semicontinuity.
3. (Rescaled balls.) For ρ > 0, g_ρ = h_ρ·c_ρ⁻¹ with the constant c_ρ⁻¹ ∈ (0, ∞). Multiplication by a finite constant is a continuous monotone self-map of [0, ∞], so it preserves lower semicontinuity (Continuous.comp_lowerSemicontinuous with a monotone outer map; ENNReal.continuous_div_const needs only c_ρ ≠ 0). Hence g_ρ is lower semicontinuous for every ρ > 0.
4. (Truncated suprema.) For ε > 0 let G_ε(x) := sup_{ρ ∈ (0, ε)} g_ρ(x). A pointwise supremum of lower semicontinuous functions is lower semicontinuous (lowerSemicontinuous_iSup / lowerSemicontinuous_biSup), so each G_ε is lower semicontinuous. Each set {G_ε > t} is then open, so G_ε is Borel measurable (LowerSemicontinuous.measurable). Only ρ > 0 enters G_ε.
5. (limsup as a countable infimum.) The intervals (0, ε), ε > 0, form a basis of 𝓝[>]0. By Filter.HasBasis.limsup_eq_iInf_iSup, Θ*(x) = inf_{ε>0} G_ε(x). G_ε(x) is non-decreasing in ε. Each 1/(m+1) is positive, so inf_{ε>0} G_ε(x) ≤ inf_{m∈ℕ} G_{1/(m+1)}(x). Conversely, for every ε > 0 there is m with 1/(m+1) < ε, and then G_{1/(m+1)}(x) ≤ G_ε(x). Hence Θ*(x) = inf_{m∈ℕ} G_{1/(m+1)}(x). Equivalently, apply the basis lemma to a countable basis of 𝓝[>]0 indexed by m ∈ ℕ, e.g. the sets B_{1/(m+1)}(0) ∩ (0, ∞) (nhdsWithin_hasBasis Metric.nhds_basis_ball_inv_nat_succ).
6. (Conclusion.) x ↦ Θ*(x) is a countable infimum of the Borel functions G_{1/(m+1)} (step 4), so it is Borel measurable (Measurable.iInf). ENNReal.toReal is measurable (ENNReal.measurable_toReal), so x ↦ Θ*(x).toReal is Borel measurable. ∎
proof_key_steps: ω_n ∈ (0, ∞), so c_ρ = ω_nρ^n ∈ (0, ∞) for ρ > 0.
x ↦ μ(B_ρ(x)) is lower semicontinuous by continuity from below on the balls B_{s}(x), s ↑ ρ.
Dividing by c_ρ and taking suprema over ρ ∈ (0, ε) preserves lower semicontinuity, so G_ε is Borel.
limsup along 𝓝[>]0 equals inf_m G_{1/(m+1)}, a countable infimum; toReal is measurable.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type agree for arbitrary measures and all natural dimensions. Continuity from below proves lower semicontinuity of ball masses; positive normalization, suprema, a countable neighbourhood-basis infimum, and measurable toReal establish the conclusion. No finiteness assumption or circular reliance is hidden.
